end.summary:
Practised estimating a large collection using groups of 10 as a guide.
Ananya identified that 30 is 3 tens and used counting by tens.
They explained estimation as using a known part to guess the whole without counting everything.
They sometimes judged quantity by how spread out objects looked; this was not corrected by the end.
The mix-up of counting groups as single objects was corrected later using 3 groups of 9 = 27, close to 30.
end.parentNote: Asha practised grouping objects in tens and using a known group to estimate a larger collection. Ananya explained the method as making a close guess from one known part, and they corrected the group-counting mix-up by connecting 3 groups of 9 with about 30. The idea that spreading objects makes the collection larger still needs practice. At home, make two rows with the same number of items—one spread out and one close together—and ask Ananya to estimate and then check by counting.
